info.title: TaskFlow API
info.description: Implemented v1 project-based MVP plus opt-in workspace v2 read/write preview (WorkspaceReads:Enabled and WorkspaceWrites:Enabled, both default false). UI cutover, lifecycle roles and expectedVersion remain pending. Session cookies are HttpOnly; CSRF requires cookie plus header. Local versus Strict security alternatives describe deployment modes, not interchangeable cookies accepted by one deployment. Transport:RequireHttps selects cookie names; public HTTPS is the hosted default. Unknown/repeated collection query parameters are rejected case-insensitively; Enums and dynamic task PATCH field names are case-sensitive; typed body binding accepts name casing variants.

get.description: Responses include X-Trace-Id and Cache-Control: no-store. IDs remain decimal strings. Inaccessible/deleted resources return 404; visible forbidden operations return 403 where applicable. Account-security mail preview is default off and restricted to Development/Staging. Email requests return the same empty 202 for absent, unverified, cooling-down and accepted accounts. Tokens are submitted in JSON, expire within one hour and are never returned by this API. Confirmation/reset rotate the security stamp and reject replay; password change signs out all sessions. Reauthentication is password-proven, five-minute and bound to the session stamp. No real email transport is enabled.

get.description: Responses include X-Trace-Id and Cache-Control: no-store. IDs remain decimal strings. Inaccessible/deleted resources return 404; visible forbidden operations return 403 where applicable. Requires all workspace rollout flags and Invitations:Enabled (default false). Company Owner/Admin can invite Member/Guest; Editor/Viewer invitations require both company Owner/Admin and current private-project ownership. The API never returns raw tokens or token hashes. Intended verified recipient and current inviter authority are checked under the workspace gate. Pending invitations reserve company seats; acceptance consumes a one-use SHA-256 token and commits grants/audit atomically. Resend rotates the token without extending expiry, requires expectedVersion, one-minute cooldown and at most three resends. No UI or real mail provider is enabled by this foundation.

parameters.name: X-Expected-Version
parameters.description: Revision returned by the loaded record, as a positive canonical decimal string within signed BIGINT.
